questions.title: An audit does not start on audit day. It starts with the questions you ask every week.
questions.lead: Anyone who works in compliance knows the scene: the document exists, but nobody remembers which control it proves. The answer is out there, scattered across spreadsheets, folders and chats. Every question turns into a search, an email or a meeting.

items.q: Which control does this document prove?
items.before: Open the control spreadsheet and hope it is up to date.
items.after: The evidence already sits inside the control it proves.

items.before: Check dates file by file, or find out on the day.
items.after: The renewal queue shows what has expired and what is about to.

items.q: Who is behind on a fix?
items.before: A round of emails and a follow-up meeting.
items.after: Every gap becomes an action with an owner, a deadline and a status.

items.before: An opinion put together in a rush during audit week.
items.after: A current score from 0 to 100%, with what weighs most against it.

items.q: Where did we stop last cycle?
items.before: Rebuild the history from old folders.
items.after: History, versions and audit trail are kept.

how.title: Everything connected, from requirement to score.
how.p1: Each requirement of the standard becomes a control; each control has the evidence that proves it. When something is missing, the gap becomes an action with an owner and a deadline, and the score shows the effect.
how.p2: The journey has seven stages, each with an exit condition that the system itself checks. You do not find out the day before that an earlier phase was left incomplete.

market.title: Certification has become a common language between companies, and between countries.
market.text: It is the fastest way for a buyer to trust a supplier it has never audited. Earning the certificate opens doors; keeping it alive, cycle after cycle, is where the team's time goes.

bids.label: Public tenders in Brazil
bids.title: Certification earns points and, when justified, can be required.
bids.text: Brazil's Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) accepts scoring certifications in technique-and-price tenders. Under Law 14.133/2021, the court has found it lawful to require ISO certification at qualification when the need is technically demonstrated (Ruling 1091/2025). The general rule is still not to restrict competition.

intl.label: International markets
intl.title: Foreign customers ask for proof, not promises.
intl.text: In the European Union, NIS2 requires entities to manage supply chain security (art. 21). In the United Kingdom, central government requires Cyber Essentials from suppliers on contracts involving personal data or IT systems.

meta.title: Platform
meta.description: Assessment by requirement, controls and SOA, evidence with expiry dates, plans and actions, audits and CAPA, reports and LGPD in one place.

platform.title: Requirements, controls, evidence and actions in one place.
platform.lead: ARS organizes compliance work around the standard that matters to you. Every piece is linked to the next, and the Audit Readiness Score shows, at any moment, how far you are from your readiness target.

score.title: A calculated number, not an impression.
score.text: The score runs from 0 to 100% and is calculated from the standard's controls, with more weight for the most critical ones. The readiness target is 85%. When evidence expires or an action falls behind, the number shows it.

features.title: Assessment by requirement
features.text: Each requirement of the standard is assessed at the start of the journey. The result becomes the starting point of the plan, with the gaps already identified.

features.title: Controls and SOA
features.text: Controls linked to the requirements they meet, with applicability and justification recorded. The Statement of Applicability comes straight out of the platform.

features.title: Evidence with an owner and an expiry date
features.text: Upload, approval, versions and expiry date. Expired evidence goes into a renewal queue with a 15-day grace period, before the control is left uncovered.

features.title: Plans and actions
features.text: Every gap becomes an action with an owner, a deadline and a status. What has been completed shows up in the score.

features.title: Audits and CAPA
features.text: Findings and nonconformities are recorded, with corrective action and follow-up until closure.

features.title: Ready-made reports
features.text: Readiness, SOA, Evidence and Maturity reports, in PDF or Excel, for the internal meeting or for the auditor.

features.title: Brazil's LGPD in the same environment
features.text: Records of processing activities (ROPA), data protection impact assessments, incidents and data subject requests, next to the security controls.

features.title: Audit trail
features.text: Every change is recorded, with version history. The record cannot be edited afterwards.

meta.title: How it works
meta.description: Requirement, control, evidence, gap, action and score: how ARS connects every piece and guides the seven-stage journey to the audit.

how.title: From requirement to score, a chain that does not break.
how.lead: Audit readiness depends on knowing, for each requirement of the standard, what meets it, what proves it and what is still missing. ARS keeps that chain connected from start to finish.

chain.d: What the standard asks for. It is where everything starts.
How the organization meets the requirement, with an owner and applicability.
The document or record that proves the control, with an expiry date.
What is missing for the control to be considered met.
The fix for the gap, with an owner, a deadline and a status.
The effect of all this on the Audit Readiness Score, weighted by the control's criticality.

how.journeyTitle: Seven stages to the audit, and beyond
how.journeyLead: Each stage has an exit condition that the system itself checks. You do not find out the day before that an earlier phase was left incomplete.

stages.d: Each requirement of the chosen standard is assessed.
Gaps become actions with owners and deadlines.
Controls are put in place and evidence is submitted.
Final check against the readiness target.
External audit and recording of the result.
Renewals, surveillance audits and the next cycle.

faq.a: No. The certification body decides on certification. ARS organizes, records and tracks the preparation and the cycle that follows.

faq.q: Does ARS replace the consultant or the auditor?
faq.a: No. ARS is the platform where the work happens. Consultants, internal auditors and the external auditor can work inside it.
The catalog has 37 standards and frameworks, with 706 requirements, including ISO 27001, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 22301, ISO 27701, ISO 42001 and LGPD.
It goes into a renewal queue with a 15-day grace period. During that time, the control still counts in the internal score, but not in what the external auditor sees.

faq.q: Can the external auditor access ARS?
faq.a: Yes. The external auditor can have their own access, with a defined scope, to review what they need without waiting for files to be sent.

cert.typicalTitle: What an ISO certification cycle usually looks like
cert.typical: For most certifiable ISO standards, the certificate is valid for three years, with surveillance audits in between and recertification at the end of the cycle. The exact schedule is set by the certification body.

frameworks.soc2: SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a certification. LGPD, NIS2 and DORA are regulations.

meta.title: Security
meta.description: The principles ARS applies to your organization's compliance data: isolation, an immutable audit trail and verified evidence.

security.title: Traceability by default.
security.lead: Compliance depends on reliable records. These are the principles ARS applies to your organization's data.

items.d: Each organization's information is isolated from other organizations.
Records are append-only and chained by hash, so any later change becomes evident.
On upload, ARS checks the file's real type, its size and the hash of its content.
The external auditor sees only what was granted to them, for the period you set.
Evidence and documents keep their previous versions, cycle after cycle.
Each person signs in with their own account, and what they do is recorded in their name.
